prov_p132.name: Khê Thanh
prov_p132.lore: Grass, forest and steppe along a clear chattering brook that runs to the bay. Its villagers keep the banks clean for Thiên Bảo Trai, which rinses its finest refinings here. On the steppe shore lie the burned walls of Hoa Ổ Viện, a hall of Lạc Anh Phái lost in the fighting for the Petal Shore.

prov_p133.name: Khê Đầu
prov_p133.lore: Open grass where the brook rises from a carp-head spout, with the burned ruins of Kim Cốc Thành and Hồng Vũ Thành on its land. Its villagers guard the spring and herd a few cattle. Hornets nest in the old walls, and the scavengers who sift Kim Cốc's ash go in with smoke pots.

prov_p134.name: Hải Môn
prov_p134.lore: Grass, bamboo and a little jungle on the bay coast by the great rock arch. Its fishers time everything by the tide through the arch. Troops of spirit monkeys live in the bamboo hills and raid the drying racks.

prov_p135.name: Tân Khẩu
prov_p135.lore: Grass and bamboo round the harbour mouth where the refugees of Vô Định Thành settled in 805. Its people fish and keep their blank wall turned to the plain. A hot spring behind the village is called the spring of forgetting, and the old ones bathe there in silence.

prov_p39.name: Tử Điện
prov_p39.lore: Grass and bamboo round Tử Điện Thành, Lạc Hà's armoury city on the bay, where a river meets the sea. Its people are smiths, guards and fishers, the most disciplined in the bay. In the bamboo hills behind the city a Wood vein runs under a grove of purple-stemmed bamboo.

prov_p50.name: Vật Hoa
prov_p50.lore: Dry steppe, red badlands and a river below Thiên Bảo Trai, around the market of the land's riches. Its people are traders, carters and caravan guards. Scorpions as long as a forearm live in the badland gullies, and the market sells their venom to alchemists.

prov_p76.name: Liễu Ngạn
prov_p76.lore: Grass and forest on a flooding river behind the willow levee. Its people farm the flood land and beat the drum when the river passes the red mark. Giant spirit turtles haul out on the river shoals, and the levee guards keep an eye on them as well as on the water.

prov_p77.name: Hòa Phong
prov_p77.lore: Almost all open grass on the bay coast, swept by the gentle sea breeze. Its people keep guesthouses for the sick and fish the bay. An orchid-scented Wood vein in the grass inland is where its healers sit before they treat the gravely ill.

prov_p78.name: Ngũ Cốc
prov_p78.lore: Grass and bamboo round Ngũ Cốc Thành, the bay's grain port. Its people are guildsmen, porters and the descendants of Kim Cốc merchants. Spirit rats as large as dogs burrow on the rise behind the granaries, and every grain guild pays a rat-catcher.

prov_thien_bao.name: Thiên Bảo
prov_thien_bao.lore: Red badlands and dry steppe round the seat of Thiên Bảo Trai, with the red gold mine of Xích Kim and the burned ruin of Vô Định Thành at the edge of the poisoned plain. Its people are refiners, miners and furnace hands. A Metal vein on the badlands shines at night like buried swords, and the Trai guards it closely.

prov_r12_1.name: Hoàng Trần Hoang
prov_r12_1.lore: High dry badlands and steppe with a few bare peaks, where the wind lifts yellow dust every afternoon. No one lives here; there is no water and the poisoned plain lies not far beyond its hills. Thiên Bảo's prospectors cross it for the Earth vein on its high steppe and leave before dark.

prov_r12_10.name: Viên Nhật Nguyên
prov_r12_10.lore: Dry steppe and desert under high bare mountains on the border with Thính Vũ Lâu. No one lives here but Lạc Hà's watch on the ridge of Trường Hà Mạch. The plain takes its name from the same line as the vein, the long river and the round setting sun, which here sinks straight into the flat land.

prov_r12_11.name: Thu Tân
prov_r12_11.lore: Steppe and grass rising from the bay shore to high bare mountains. Its villagers fish the shore and graze goats on the slopes. An Earth vein high on the steppe is wrapped most mornings in ranks of mist.

prov_r12_12.name: Đào Ẩn
prov_r12_12.lore: Inland grass, jungle and bamboo behind Tử Điện Thành. Its villagers grow longans and send them to the bay cities in summer. Peach trees still fruit wild among the jungle here, from the orchards of the Petal Shore.

prov_r12_13.name: Ngư Võng
prov_r12_13.lore: Coastal grass with jungle along the bay, beside the web-hung wood of Thiên Chu Lâm. Its villagers fish with nets and mend them on the beach. No sect holds the spider wood, and the villagers burn back its edge every spring.

prov_r12_14.name: Hoàng Long
prov_r12_14.lore: Open grass on the bay coast, flat and low. Its town builds and paints the dragon prows of the bay's ships. A Water vein near the shore runs under a spring-fed stream that never fails in drought.

prov_r12_15.name: Châu Liêm
prov_r12_15.lore: Grass and jungle along the bay coast. Its town strings shell beads into curtains that hang in every rich house of the bay. A hot spring inland is where its bead-drillers rest their eyes.

prov_r12_2.name: Liệt Nham Lĩnh
prov_r12_2.lore: Badlands and high split crags, with no water and no roads. No one lives here but iron miners in summer. Its high peak can be seen from Thiên Bảo Trai, and the poisoned plain lies beyond its far side.

prov_r12_3.name: Hàn Nham Lĩnh
prov_r12_3.lore: High cold mountains above the badlands, the highest ground in the bay's lands. No one lives here; only jade cutters climb up in summer. Thiên Bảo Trai buys every stone they bring down.

prov_r12_4.name: Liên Chu
prov_r12_4.lore: Dry steppe with badland gullies along a river. Its villagers keep the pontoon bridge that carries the caravan road to Vật Hoa Thị. Giant lizards bask on the gully rocks and take stray goats.

prov_r12_5.name: Mã Độ
prov_r12_5.lore: Steppe and grass along a river where horses can wade across. Its villagers breed hardy steppe ponies and sell them to the caravans. Herds of wild spirit asses run on the steppe and kick any rider who comes too close.

prov_r12_6.name: Hàm Phong
prov_r12_6.lore: Dry steppe on the bay coast, swept by a salty wind. Its villagers fish and dry their catch in the wind. A hot spring inland runs red over the rocks.

prov_r12_7.name: Bạch Dương
prov_r12_7.lore: Wide steppe with patches of grass and desert, from the bay coast far inland. Its herders run white sheep between wells. On the coast stands Minh Loan Các, whose ward bells ring on the bay's ships and the caravans.

prov_r12_8.name: Hà Khúc
prov_r12_8.lore: Steppe and grass along a winding river. Its villagers farm the bends and fish the pools. Golden eagles nest on the high ground and take lambs.

prov_r12_9.name: Xích Thổ
prov_r12_9.lore: Steppe, desert and salt flats along a river that runs to the sea, rising to bare heights. Its villagers farm the red earth by the river and gather salt from the brine lake. Herders avoid the far heights, which look toward the poisoned plain.

prov_p132_spirit_vein_1.name: Chu Hoa Mạch
prov_p132_spirit_vein_1.look: A wood by the brook where red flowers grow on the forest floor all year.
prov_p132_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Wood vein runs under the wood, named for the old line about vermilion blooms by the water. Thiên Bảo's apprentices rest here between rinsings.

prov_p132_ruin_2.name: Hoa Ổ Viện
prov_p132_ruin_2.look: Burned walls and a fallen gate on the steppe shore, with a few old peach trees still growing in the empty courtyard.
prov_p132_ruin_2.lore: Lạc Anh Phái built this hall in 280 to graft its peach trees. When Lạc Hà and Thính Vũ fought over the empty Petal Shore it burned with the orchards in 618, and no one rebuilt it. The peach trees in its courtyard still flower each spring.

prov_p133_beast_lair_1.name: Độc Phong Nguyên
prov_p133_beast_lair_1.look: Open grass by the brook head where the air hums and grey paper nests hang from every bush.
prov_p133_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit hornets as long as a thumb nest here, and a dozen stings can kill. The villagers of Khê Đầu smoke them back from the spring each summer.

prov_p134_beast_lair_1.name: Quần Hầu Lĩnh
prov_p134_beast_lair_1.look: A bamboo ridge loud with chattering, where the canes bend under the weight of monkeys.
prov_p134_beast_lair_1.lore: Troops of spirit monkeys live in the bamboo and raid the fish racks of Hải Môn. They throw stones well enough to break a skull, and the fishers keep dogs.

prov_p135_hot_spring_1.name: Vong Ưu Tuyền
prov_p135_hot_spring_1.look: A clear warm pool in the grass behind the village, with a single stone bench beside it.
prov_p135_hot_spring_1.lore: The refugees of Vô Định Thành called it the spring of forgetting. The old ones bathe there in silence, and no one speaks while they are in the water.

prov_p39_spirit_vein_1.name: Tử Trúc Mạch
prov_p39_spirit_vein_1.look: A grove of purple-stemmed bamboo in the hills behind the city, its canes dark as old lacquer.
prov_p39_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Wood vein runs under the grove, and its bamboo grows purple only here. The armoury of Tử Điện cuts it for arrow shafts and keeps a guard on the grove.

prov_p50_beast_lair_1.name: Hạt Vĩ Cương
prov_p50_beast_lair_1.look: A dry steppe ridge whose rocks are pocked with burrows and littered with cast-off shells.
prov_p50_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit scorpions as long as a forearm live here. The venom gatherers of Vật Hoa Thị catch them at night with lamps and sell the venom to alchemists.

prov_p76_beast_lair_1.name: Bạch Miết Chử
prov_p76_beast_lair_1.look: Grassy shoals on the river where huge flat shells lie in the sun like stepping stones.
prov_p76_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit soft-shelled turtles as wide as a door haul out here. Their bite takes off a hand, and the levee guards of Liễu Ngạn chase them back into the river when they come near the levee.

prov_p77_spirit_vein_1.name: Huệ Phong Mạch
prov_p77_spirit_vein_1.look: A hollow in the open grass where wild orchids grow and the breeze carries their scent toward the town.
prov_p77_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Wood vein runs under the hollow, and the healers of Hòa Phong sit here before they treat the gravely ill. They say the breeze over it carries its qi to the sick.

prov_p78_beast_lair_1.name: Thạc Thử Cương
prov_p78_beast_lair_1.look: A low grassy rise behind the granaries, honeycombed with burrows as wide as a barrel.
prov_p78_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit rats as large as dogs burrow here and raid the grain towers at night, as in the old song of the great rats. Every grain guild of Ngũ Cốc pays its own rat-catcher and blames the others' rats.

prov_thien_bao_spirit_vein_1.name: Long Quang Mạch
prov_thien_bao_spirit_vein_1.look: A high badland ridge where at night a pale light rises from cracks in the red rock, like the glow of buried swords.
prov_thien_bao_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Metal vein runs under the ridge, named for the old line in which the dragon light of buried swords shoots up at the stars. Thiên Bảo Trai holds it and lets its refiners cultivate here before great workings.

prov_r12_1_spirit_vein_1.name: Ốc Thổ Mạch
prov_r12_1_spirit_vein_1.look: A broad shelf of high steppe among the badlands where the soil lies deep and dark among bare red rock.
prov_r12_1_spirit_vein_1.lore: A heavy Earth vein runs under the shelf, the only green ground for a day's walk. Thiên Bảo's prospectors cultivate here on their way through and never stay the night.

prov_r12_11_village_1.name: Thu Tân Thôn
prov_r12_11_village_1.look: A fishing village on the bay shore below bare hills, its boats drawn up on a gravel beach.
prov_r12_11_village_1.lore: Its villagers fish the bay in autumn when the water runs clearest and graze goats on the hills the rest of the year. The bay is said to be most like its name here.

prov_r12_11_spirit_vein_2.name: Vụ Liệt Mạch
prov_r12_11_spirit_vein_2.look: A high steppe shoulder where the morning mists lie in long even ranks along the slope.
prov_r12_11_spirit_vein_2.lore: An Earth vein runs under the shoulder, and its qi holds the mists in place until noon. Lạc Hà's disciples climb up to cultivate in the mist.

prov_r12_12_village_1.name: Đào Ẩn Thôn
prov_r12_12_village_1.look: A village in a jungle clearing ringed by longan orchards, heavy with brown fruit in summer.
prov_r12_12_village_1.lore: Its villagers grow longans and dry them on bamboo trays for the bay cities. Wild peaches from the old Petal Shore orchards grow among their trees.

prov_r12_12_spirit_vein_2.name: Thúy Bình Mạch
prov_r12_12_spirit_vein_2.look: A grassy rise backed by a wall of jungle that stands like a green screen.
prov_r12_12_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Wood vein runs under the rise. The villagers of Đào Ẩn say their trees fruit best on the side facing it.

prov_r12_13_village_1.name: Ngư Võng Thôn
prov_r12_13_village_1.look: A fishing village on the jungle shore where nets hang drying on poles all along the beach.
prov_r12_13_village_1.lore: Its villagers fish with nets and burn back the edge of Thiên Chu Lâm each spring. They say a spider web and a net are the same thing, and that the village must stay quicker.

prov_r12_14_town_1.name: Hoàng Long Trấn
prov_r12_14_town_1.look: A small walled town on the flat coast whose slipways hold half-carved dragon prows painted yellow.
prov_r12_14_town_1.lore: Its name comes from the old line about ships with blue bird and yellow dragon prows. Its carvers make the prows for the bay's ships, and a ship launched without one is thought unlucky.

prov_r12_14_spirit_vein_2.name: Lưu Thủy Mạch
prov_r12_14_spirit_vein_2.look: A spring-fed stream in the grass that runs clear and full even in the driest summer.
prov_r12_14_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Water vein feeds the stream, named for the old tune of flowing water. Musicians of the bay come to play beside it.

prov_r12_15_town_1.name: Châu Liêm Trấn
prov_r12_15_town_1.look: A small walled town on the bay coast whose doorways all hang with curtains of shell beads that click in the wind.
prov_r12_15_town_1.lore: Its drillers string shell beads into curtains for the rich houses of the bay, after the old line about pearl curtains rolled up at dusk. A bride's curtain takes her family a year to make.

prov_r12_15_hot_spring_2.name: Ngọc Lộ Thang
prov_r12_15_hot_spring_2.look: A warm spring in the grass whose steam leaves beads of dew on the reeds around it.
prov_r12_15_hot_spring_2.lore: The bead-drillers of Châu Liêm bathe their tired eyes in the water. They say it keeps an old driller's sight sharp.

prov_r12_2_peak_1.name: Trùng Tiêu Phong
prov_r12_2_peak_1.look: A sheer grey peak above the badlands whose tip often stands above the clouds.
prov_r12_2_peak_1.lore: Its name comes from the old line about peaks rising above the layered heavens. Its bare rock carries Metal qi, and Thiên Bảo's refiners climb it to temper blades in its cold wind.

prov_r12_2_mine_2.name: Mặc Thiết Khoáng
prov_r12_2_mine_2.look: Adits cut into a high crag, their spoil heaps black against the red badlands.
prov_r12_2_mine_2.lore: Miners dig black iron here in summer and carry it down on mules to Thiên Bảo's furnaces. In winter the mine is shut and the wind has it.

prov_r12_3_peak_1.name: Tằng Loan Phong
prov_r12_3_peak_1.look: A tall square-sided peak of pale rock, the highest in the bay's lands, standing above ridge after ridge.
prov_r12_3_peak_1.lore: Its name comes from the old line about layered ranges rising green to the heavens. Its rock carries Metal and Earth qi, and few cultivators have climbed it.

prov_r12_3_mine_2.name: Lam Ngọc Khoáng
prov_r12_3_mine_2.look: A cold high working where blue-green jade shows in the rock face under a crust of frost.
prov_r12_3_mine_2.lore: Jade cutters climb up each summer and work until the first snow. Thiên Bảo Trai buys every stone they bring down and sells the best at its auctions.

prov_r12_4_village_1.name: Liên Chu Thôn
prov_r12_4_village_1.look: A steppe village on a river where a bridge of boats lashed together carries the caravan road.
prov_r12_4_village_1.lore: Its villagers keep the pontoon bridge and take a small toll for Thiên Bảo Trai. When the river floods they cut the bridge loose and haul it back afterwards.

prov_r12_4_beast_lair_2.name: Hoàng Tích Cương
prov_r12_4_beast_lair_2.look: A ridge of yellow rock in the steppe where great lizards lie motionless in the sun.
prov_r12_4_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit lizards as long as a cart bask here and take stray goats and sheep. Their hides are sold to Thiên Bảo's armourers.

prov_r12_5_village_1.name: Mã Độ Thôn
prov_r12_5_village_1.look: A steppe village by a shallow river ford, its corrals full of shaggy ponies.
prov_r12_5_village_1.lore: Its villagers breed hardy steppe ponies and sell them to the caravans. A caravan that buys its ponies here is said never to lose one to thirst.

prov_r12_5_beast_lair_2.name: Dã Lư Nguyên
prov_r12_5_beast_lair_2.look: Open steppe crossed by dusty trails and the dung heaps of wild herds.
prov_r12_5_beast_lair_2.lore: Herds of wild spirit asses run here, fast as a horse and vicious. They kick riders from the saddle and kill ponies that stray into the herd.

prov_r12_6_village_1.name: Hàm Phong Thôn
prov_r12_6_village_1.look: A fishing village on the steppe coast where racks of split fish dry in a constant salty wind.
prov_r12_6_village_1.lore: Its fish dry in the salt wind in a single day, and the bay's caravans buy them for the road.

prov_r12_6_hot_spring_2.name: Lưu Đan Trì
prov_r12_6_hot_spring_2.look: A hot pool in the steppe whose overflow runs down the rocks in a bright red stain.
prov_r12_6_hot_spring_2.lore: Its name comes from the old line about vermilion flowing from the pavilion's eaves. Its iron water stains the rocks red, and the fishers soak their sore joints in it.

prov_r12_7_village_1.name: Bạch Dương Thôn
prov_r12_7_village_1.look: A cluster of felt tents and stone pens around a deep well on the open steppe.
prov_r12_7_village_1.lore: Its herders run white sheep between the wells of the steppe and sell the wool at Vật Hoa Thị. They move camp by the stars.

prov_r12_7_hot_spring_2.name: Kim Sa Tuyền
prov_r12_7_hot_spring_2.look: A warm spring in the steppe whose bed glitters with golden grains of mica.
prov_r12_7_hot_spring_2.lore: Prospectors once dug the spring for gold and found only mica. The herders of Bạch Dương water their sheep here in winter.

prov_r12_7_minor_seat_p.name: Minh Loan Các
prov_r12_7_minor_seat_p.look: A tall pavilion on the steppe shore, its eaves hung with hundreds of bronze bells that ring together in the sea wind.
prov_r12_7_minor_seat_p.lore: Bell-casters founded the pavilion in 960 under Lạc Hà Tông, after the old line about jade pendants and singing bells. Its disciples cast ward bells whose note drives off beasts and warns of attack, and every ship and caravan of the bay carries one. A disciple must cast a bell that rings true before learning any art.

sect.name: Minh Loan Các
sect.craft: bell casting and sound arts; ward bells for ships and caravans

prov_r12_8_village_1.name: Hà Khúc Thôn
prov_r12_8_village_1.look: A steppe village on a tight bend of the river, its fields laid out inside the loop.
prov_r12_8_village_1.lore: Its villagers farm the bend and fish the deep pools. When the river cuts a new bend, the village moves its fields and keeps its houses.

prov_r12_8_beast_lair_2.name: Hoàng Điêu Đài
prov_r12_8_beast_lair_2.look: A rocky terrace on the high steppe where great eagles sit on the stones and the ground is strewn with bones.
prov_r12_8_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit golden eagles nest here and take lambs and foals. Mục Vân Trang's riders have tried to tame their chicks and never succeeded.

prov_r12_9_village_1.name: Xích Thổ Thôn
prov_r12_9_village_1.look: A steppe village of red mud houses by a river, with salt carts lined up outside.
prov_r12_9_village_1.lore: Its villagers farm the red earth by the river and gather salt from the brine lake. They never take their flocks to the far heights.

prov_r12_9_lake_2.name: Bạch Lỗ Hồ
prov_r12_9_lake_2.look: A shallow brine lake on the salt flats, ringed with white crust and too salty for any fish.
prov_r12_9_lake_2.lore: The villagers of Xích Thổ rake salt from its shores and sell it to the caravans. Its water holds a body up like a raft.
